title: Compact-support site comparison respects compactification calculus
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$. All schemes below are finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], without a separatedness assumption on their structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Every morphism $f:X\to Y$ to which compact support is applied is separated and finite type and has a chosen compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], comparison $C_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and compact-support candidates $F_f^{e,c}=Rp_{e,*}j_!^e$, $F_f^{p,c}=Rp_{p,*}j_!^p$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Define
$$B_f^c=Rp_{p,*}(e_j)\circ\beta_{p,j_!^e}:C_YF_f^{e,c}\longrightarrow F_f^{p,c}C_X,$$
where $\beta_p$ is the counit-mate direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] and $e_j:C_{\overline X}j_!^e\cong j_!^pC_X$ is the adjoint extension-by-zero comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. On $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $B_f^c$ is invertible and has the following coherence with the canonical compactification maps. For composable separated finite-type morphisms $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ with chosen compactifications and compatible composition towers, and for two compactifications $c,c'$ of $f$ with a specified proper refinement, use the refinement comparisons $\rho^{e}_{c',c}:F_f^{e,c}\to F_f^{e,c'}$ and $\rho^p_{c',c}:F_f^{p,c}\to F_f^{p,c'}$, and composition comparisons $\alpha^e_{g,f}:F_g^eF_f^e\to F_{gf}^e$, $\alpha^p_{g,f}:F_g^pF_f^p\to F_{gf}^p$ of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons, thm-sf-comp-composition],
$$B_f^{c'}C_Y(\rho^e_{c',c})=\rho^p_{c',c}C_X\circ B_f^c,$$
$$B_{gf}C_Z(\alpha^e_{g,f})=\alpha^p_{g,f}C_X\circ(F_g^pB_f)\circ(B_gF_f^e).$$
For an open immersion $v:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ and its Cartesian pullback $u:X'\hookrightarrow X$, let $f':X'\to Y'$ be the pullback and use the pulled-back compactification. The canonical compact-support restriction exchanges $\operatorname{Ex}^e:v_e^*F_f^e\to F_{f'}^eu_e^*$ and $\operatorname{Ex}^p:v_p^*F_f^p\to F_{f'}^pu_p^*$ are invertible and obey
$$\operatorname{Ex}^p\circ v_p^*B_f=B_{f'}u_e^*\circ C_{Y'}(\operatorname{Ex}^e),$$
under the canonical pullback comparisons. All these identities use the normalized proper/open interchanges in compatible compactification towers, including commutative proper/open squares which are not Cartesian, and the counit-mate normalization above; they hold on bounded-below etale witnesses. They respect identities and pasting.

proof.text: For a refinement r:c to d, expand the etale d-to-c refinement map as the proper image of the etale proper/open map followed by the inverse proper compositor. Expand the specified pro-etale proper/open isomorphism into its four defining factors. Direct-image comparison composition, naturality of the comparison for d.g, and naturality of the pro-etale compositor identify the two expanded composites. The intermediate open comparison and its inverse cancel. Thus C(rho_etale.hom) followed by B_c equals B_d followed by the inverse actual pro-etale refinement. Invert this equation to obtain the stated c-to-d refinement square.
